root_cause: When the focused 'Show all 4 results' button is removed from the DOM, the browser moves focus to the body. The focus trap's checkFocusIn handler attempts to restore focus using the stale mostRecentlyFocusedNode (the removed button) or the initial focus node. However, the initial focus node is derived from state.tabbableGroups which is not updated after the button removal, and the focus() call during the focusin event may not take effect synchronously, causing the test to observe focus on the body before restoration occurs.
repair_strategy: Update the tabbable nodes in checkFocusIn before attempting to restore focus, and perform the focus restoration synchronously. The restoration logic will prefer the most recently focused node if it is still contained in a trap container; otherwise it will directly use the first tabbable node from the first tabbable group (which reflects the updated DOM) as a fallback, avoiding any indirection through getInitialFocusNode that might rely on stale state.
expected_accessibility_effect: After activating the trap and removing the focused node (via the 'Show all 4 results' button), keyboard focus will remain trapped within the dialog, moving to the close button (the first tabbable node) when the focused node is removed. This ensures that subsequent tab navigation remains within the dialog and the focus-within assertion passes.
functional_risks: Calling updateTabbableNodes on every focus escape adds a small performance cost, but focus escapes are rare.
If the trap is deactivated before the focus restoration runs, tryFocus will early-return because state.active is false.
Synchronous focus() during a focusin event may be ignored by some browsers, but stopping immediate propagation increases the chance of success.
verification_requirements: Verify that after clicking the 'Show all 4 results' button (which removes itself), focus is retained within the results dialog (specifically, the close button should receive focus).
Verify that tab navigation continues to work within the dialog after the button removal.
Verify that the Escape key still closes the dialog and returns focus to the open button.
Verify that the initial state of the trap (before any node removal) still functions correctly.
